programme: A p21/CDKN1A-centered cell-cycle-checkpoint and senescence module: SP1 and YBX1 activate CDKN1A directly (both list it as a target), ZBTB4 is a documented CDKN1A repressor that competes with Sp1-family activators at the same GC-box elements and also recruits the SIN3A corepressor, DMAP1 sits in the Tip60/NuA4-ATM DNA-damage axis and lists CDKN1A, BAX and ATM among its five targets, TCF3 (E2A) also binds CDKN1A, and RCOR2 extends the same checkpoint logic to the CDKN1A paralog CDKN2B via the CoREST repressor complex.
role_in_a: In Alzheimer's disease, SP1 is repeatedly documented as a driver of AD-related transcriptional pathology, ZBTB4 variants track with age-at-onset (tying checkpoint control directly to disease timing), and RCOR2 loss is described in senescent, inflammaging tissue in an AD context — together consistent with a p21-driven cell-cycle-arrest/senescence programme operating in aging neurons and glia.
role_in_b: No retrieved evidence places any of these factors in pheochromocytoma or paraganglioma specifically. By general tumor-suppressor logic, chromaffin/paraganglial neuroendocrine cells depend on CDKN1A/CDKN2B-mediated growth arrest to stay post-mitotic, so loss or bypass of this same checkpoint module would be expected to permit tumor proliferation — but this is inference, not something in the record.
shared_axis: Both AD-affected neural tissue and PPGL tumor tissue are contexts where a small repressor/activator set decides whether a CDKN1A/CDKN2B checkpoint is engaged (favoring senescence/arrest, relevant to AD) or disengaged (favoring proliferation, relevant to tumor growth in PPGL); the same activator-repressor pairing (SP1/YBX1 vs ZBTB4, with DMAP1 linking to ATM damage signaling) could plausibly be redeployed at both ends of that switch.
reasoning: The module is nameable directly from the given target lists (five of six carrying factors converge on CDKN1A or CDKN2B) and most carrying factors have independent AD literature support, so this is not a guess built from nothing. But the connection to disease B rests entirely on general checkpoint-biology reasoning, since not one retrieved item — PMID or Open Targets score — places any carrying factor in pheochromocytoma or paraganglioma, and brain/adrenal is not an obviously linked tissue pair.
support: 42004890 (SP1's multifaceted roles in AD pathogenesis); 41329263 (multi-ancestry GWAS meta-analysis implicating SP1 in AD); 41969962 (SP1 mRNA expression altered in AD cases); 29045054 (ZBTB4-regulating variants associated with AD age-at-onset); 25051986 (Rcor2 underexpression in senescent mice, discussed as an inflammaging/AD-relevant target); 40311462 (YBX1 used in an AD biomarker autoencoder framework, weak/indirect); 38135866 and 25680440 (TCF3 discussed via Wnt target-gene signaling in AD — supports TCF3 in AD generally but through the Wnt axis, not the CDKN1A convergence described here). none found for Pheochromocytoma_and_Paraganglioma.
how_to_falsify: ChIP (or CUT&RUN) for SP1, YBX1, ZBTB4, DMAP1, TCF3 and RCOR2 at the CDKN1A/CDKN2B loci in matched AD-model neurons/glia versus PPGL tumor lines (e.g. PC12, hPheo1): if ZBTB4 does not occupy the same CDKN1A elements as SP1/YBX1, or if CDKN1A/CDKN2B levels do not track with senescence markers in AD tissue or with proliferative index in PPGL tumors, the shared-checkpoint account fails.
caveats: Tissue pairing is brain vs adrenal, and the 80 patient-group comparisons rest on only 6 independent cohort pairs, so replication depth is more limited than the comparison count suggests. SF1 also appears among the concordant factors with a classic adrenal-cortex steroidogenic target set (NR0B1, CYP11A1, HSD3B2, STAR, MC2R) that fits cortical, not chromaffin/medullary, biology — it is not part of the programme described here and its presence should not be read as PPGL-specific support. Tissue-generic exclusions removed SOX10, NOTCH1 and TAL1 — the more obvious neural-crest/hematopoietic master regulators — which is why this account is built on the CDKN1A convergence rather than a neural-crest developmental story; single-view exclusions (ARX, LHX3, NR0B2 and other adrenal/pituitary developmental factors) show that lineage-specific signal did not generalize across cohorts. No PMID or meaningful Open Targets association places any carrying factor in disease B.
